boundary_rationale: The row opens at 8:1 on the peri de formula Περὶ δὲ τῶν εἰδωλοθύτων (rp:1Cor.8.1), read the same in SBLGNT, which names the new subject of food offered to idols. Behind the seam, 7:40 ends the counsel on marriage with the opinion formula δοκῶ δὲ κἀγὼ (rp:1Cor.7.40), so the onset is supported from both sides. Inside the row the argument runs from knowledge and love (8:1-8:3) through the confession of one God (8:4-8:6) to the weak conscience (8:7-8:12), and it resolves in Διόπερ (rp:1Cor.8.13) with Paul's own policy οὐ μὴ φάγω κρέα (rp:1Cor.8.13). The close falls after 8:13 because 9:1 turns without a connective to Paul's own standing, Οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐλεύθερος (rp:1Cor.9.1). The word for idol food stands at 8:1, 8:4, 8:7 and 8:10 inside the row (MEASURED, script measure_w3: 6 RP verses book-wide, 5 in SBLGNT). The slogan extent contested at 8:1 is whether the quoted position is πάντες γνῶσιν ἔχομεν (rp:1Cor.8.1) alone or the clause οἴδαμεν ὅτι πάντες γνῶσιν ἔχομεν (rp:1Cor.8.1), with Ἡ γνῶσις φυσιοῖ (rp:1Cor.8.1) as Paul's reply. At 8:4 the candidate extent covers the two clauses οἴδαμεν ὅτι οὐδὲν εἴδωλον ἐν κόσμῳ (rp:1Cor.8.4) and καὶ ὅτι οὐδεὶς θεὸς ἕτερος εἰ μὴ εἷς (rp:1Cor.8.4), or the second clause alone. SBLGNT reads καὶ ὅτι οὐδεὶς ⸀θεὸς εἰ μὴ εἷς (sbl:1Cor.8.4), without the RP word ἕτερος (rp:1Cor.8.4). At 8:8 the slogan may be Βρῶμα δὲ ἡμᾶς οὐ παρίστησιν τῷ θεῷ (rp:1Cor.8.8) alone or the whole verse, and SBLGNT reads ⸀παραστήσει (sbl:1Cor.8.8) for the RP present tense. The extents stay open; they bear on the reading of the argument and do not move a seam, since no seam falls after 8:1, 8:4 or 8:8. The row spans the whole chapter of 13 verses, so its confidence is capped at the chapter-fallback level even though the onset and close rest on wording.

boundary_rationale: The row opens at 9:1 with asyndetic questions, Οὐκ εἰμὶ ἀπόστολος (rp:1Cor.9.1) and Οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐλεύθερος (rp:1Cor.9.1), which turn from the idol-food case to Paul's own rights. The freedom question answers the right named at 8:9, ἡ ἐξουσία ὑμῶν αὕτη (rp:1Cor.8.9), so 9:1 sits inside the idol-food argument as an example and not as a new subject. Behind the seam the resolve Διόπερ (rp:1Cor.8.13) closes the case of the weak conscience. SBLGNT reads the two questions in the other order, with Οὐκ εἰμὶ ⸂ἐλεύθερος (sbl:1Cor.9.1) leading. The defence word Ἡ ἐμὴ ἀπολογία (rp:1Cor.9.3) stands at 9:3 (MEASURED, script measure_w3: 1 verse book-wide in RP and SBLGNT). The appeal Οὐκ οἴδατε (rp:1Cor.9.13) at 9:13 adds a temple warrant inside the row and does not open a new move. The row closes at 9:14 on the command of the Lord, Οὕτως καὶ ὁ κύριος διέταξεν (rp:1Cor.9.14), which ends the run of warrants for the right to support. Across the seam Ἐγὼ δὲ οὐδενὶ ἐχρησάμην τούτων (rp:1Cor.9.15) turns to Paul's non-use of the right, which Ἀλλ’ οὐκ ἐχρησάμεθα τῇ ἐξουσίᾳ ταύτῃ (rp:1Cor.9.12) at 9:12 previews. Typing as example is held open, since chapter 9 also reads as a defence of apostolic rights.

strongest_rejected_alternative: A seam at 10:24/10:25 would part the slogan and rule from the market and dinner cases, at Πᾶν τὸ ἐν μακέλλῳ πωλούμενον ἐσθίετε (rp:1Cor.10.25). It is turned down because the cases apply the rule of 10:24 and the conscience thread binds 10:25-10:29. A close-seam merge with 10:31-11:1 is also weighed, since Εἴτε οὖν (rp:1Cor.10.31) draws the conclusion of the cases, and it is turned down because the summary widens from food to conduct in general.

boundary_rationale: The row opens at 10:31 with Εἴτε οὖν (rp:1Cor.10.31), which draws the conclusion of the food cases into the charge πάντα εἰς δόξαν θεοῦ ποιεῖτε (rp:1Cor.10.31). The inference pair stands in 2 verses book-wide (MEASURED, script measure_w3). Behind the seam εὐχαριστῶ (rp:1Cor.10.30) at 10:30 ends the dinner case. The charge widens at 10:32 to Jews, Greeks and τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ (rp:1Cor.10.32), and 10:33 grounds it in Paul's own practice, καθὼς κἀγὼ (rp:1Cor.10.33) and μὴ ζητῶν τὸ ἐμαυτοῦ συμφέρον (rp:1Cor.10.33). SBLGNT reads ⸀σύμφορον (sbl:1Cor.10.33) for the RP noun of that clause. The imitation charge Μιμηταί μου γίνεσθε (rp:1Cor.11.1) echoes 10:33 with καθὼς κἀγὼ χριστοῦ (rp:1Cor.11.1) (MEASURED, script measure_w3: the pair stands in 2 verses book-wide, 10:33 and 11:1, in RP and SBLGNT), so 11:1 closes the idol-food argument. Across the seam Ἐπαινῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς (rp:1Cor.11.2) opens a new subject with praise, and the RP pilcrow at 11:2 sits on that seam; the WEB paragraph start and the chapter division at 11:1 inform and do not decide.
